provenance.notes: All outputs simulated. Held-out episodes only; training episodes are listed separately. Most eval parts ran on a Colab CPU runtime (8 cores, high-RAM); see the compute field and packing-v1-parts/colab-run.json.

assumptions: Everything here is simulated; no number is a measurement of a real cluster.

Cap: each site cap is its calibrated idle power plus cap.load_fraction of the calibrated idle-to-full-load power span, both measured in the simulator at a constant design outdoor temperature (cap.design_outdoor_c). The design temperature and load fraction are assumptions chosen on calibration and dev seeds, not on test seeds.

Jobs: synthetic queue with a backlog (utilization goal above 1), GPU counts, durations (1.5 to 10 h, log-uniform), checkpoint cadence and value per GPU-hour (USD, no source) are assumptions. All jobs are marked flexible so the packer may hold them; a job is available at its submit time.

Heat wave: each episode draws a heat wave (centre, width, size) added to the sim scenario's diurnal outdoor temperature; episode time 0 is 06:00 local at the first site (start_hour_utc). The event draw rates, precursor probability and ranges are assumptions of the simulation.
Over-cap penalty (USD per kWh above the site cap) is a scenario parameter; the default and the sweep are assumptions.
Planning horizon (3 h in 5-minute steps) and the learned policy's surrogate reward window (3 h) are scenario choices.
Warm-up (first 25 h of each 41 h episode) uses one shared rule for all forecast policies and is excluded from every reported metric; the evaluation window is the last 16 h.

ETS and ARIMA refit once per hour of decisions (forecast_refresh_bins = 12) and serve the 11 decisions in between from the same paths shifted by the elapsed steps, to keep their run time down; every other forecaster is called at every decision.

Running jobs are planned to end at their declared walltime stretched by the checkpoint overhead implied by the job generator's checkpoint ranges, and count in every 5-minute bin they overlap (end_rule 'overlap').

compute.note: Eval parts other than the first 10 timestral-5M parts (run on the 2-core VM at commit dab1fd2) were produced on a Google Colab CPU runtime (session hw-pack-cpu, high-RAM shape, 8 cores reported by nproc, 50 GB RAM reported by free). 8 single-thread processes ran in parallel (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, --threads 1).
compute.hardware: Colab CPU runtime, High-RAM shape, 8 cores (nproc), about 50 GB RAM (free -g), no GPU

software.timestral: pip install git+https://github.com/mistralai/timestral.git (weights 5M and 28M from the Hugging Face hub)

compute.commands: run_packing.py eval --group {t5m-fixed | learned t28m-fixed oracle reactive seasonal-naive ets arima} --shard i/8 --n-train 6 --n-test 3 --grid-stride 2 --subset-q 0.5,0.9,0.99 --threads 1 (i = 0..7; t5m-fixed first, then the other groups)

metric_definitions.window: evaluation window = last (horizon_s - warmup_s) seconds of each episode; warm-up excluded
metric_definitions.gpu_hours: useful GPU-hours delivered in the window (net of work lost to faults), summed over jobs
metric_definitions.value_usd: sum over jobs of window GPU-hours times value per GPU-hour
metric_definitions.violation_rate: fraction of decision intervals (300 s) in the window in which any site's power exceeded its cap, at the simulator's 10 s control-step samples
metric_definitions.energy_above_cap_kwh: sum over sites and samples of the excess over the cap, in kWh
metric_definitions.seconds_above_cap: number of site-samples above the cap times the sample length, summed over sites
metric_definitions.stranded_kwh: headroom below the cap (kWh, both sites) in intervals where a queued job that fit in free GPUs was refused
metric_definitions.net_value_usd: value_usd minus penalty (USD per kWh above cap) times energy_above_cap_kwh
metric_definitions.ci: percentile bootstrap interval of the mean over held-out episodes
